item.title: King’s Lynn Rotary Club marks centenary milestone
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn Rotary Club marks centenary milestone
The Rotary Club of King’s Lynn has celebrated one hundred years of community service. Members and guests gathered at the town hall on Friday, September 25, for a black-tie dinner to mark the occasion. Around 120 people attended the event, including representatives from the club’s twin town of Emmerich-am-Rhein in Germany.
During the evening, club president Michael Douglass highlighted the group’s long-standing support for local, national, and international causes. A new book detailing the club's history, written by member Michael Walker, was also featured. Since the turn of the millennium, the organisation has provided assistance to approximately 150 charities and numerous individuals. The club says it remains committed to supporting the community for the next century.

item.title: Campaign launched to improve child road safety in the Fens
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Campaign launched to improve child road safety in the Fens
A new road safety initiative called Be Bright Be Seen has been launched across Fenland to help children stay visible as the nights draw in. Sponsored by Ashwood Homes, the campaign is distributing thousands of free reflective keyrings to local schools, sports teams, and youth groups. These can be attached to bags, coats, or bicycles to help pedestrians and cyclists stand out to motorists.
Organisers are also encouraging families to wear bright or reflective clothing during the darker months, particularly after the clocks go back on Sunday, October 25. Teachers and youth leaders can apply for a supply of the free keyrings by visiting the Fenland Citizen website.

item.title: North West Norfolk MP calls for stronger chalk stream protections
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
North West Norfolk MP calls for stronger chalk stream protections
North West Norfolk MP James Wild is calling on the government to strengthen planning protections for local chalk streams. Mr Wild has joined a cross-party group of parliamentarians in urging ministers to reconsider current planning policies, which they argue do not sufficiently safeguard these rare habitats. The campaign highlights the importance of sites in Gaywood, Babingley, and Heacham.
Supporters of the move state that chalk streams are globally scarce and require more robust legal defences against threats such as pollution and over-abstraction. Mr Wild, who is part of an All-Party Parliamentary Group focused on the issue, is advocating for clearer protections to be included in future planning decisions and the forthcoming Clean Water Bill.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/mp-urges-ministers-to-think-again-as-fight-to-protect-rare-9484820/

item.title: Former King’s Lynn student secures place at Oxford University
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Former King’s Lynn student secures place at Oxford University
A former Springwood High School student has begun his studies at the University of Oxford. Merry Enters, 18, is currently reading Philosophy, Politics and Economics at the institution. He achieved A-level results of an A* in Physics, an A in Maths, and a B in Music Technology before securing his place through a late application.
Mr. Enters credited the support of his teachers at the King’s Lynn school for encouraging his application. While he previously considered a career in music, he is now exploring future roles in economics, consulting, or analysis. He intends to continue playing the guitar as a hobby while he pursues his academic interests.

New Best Start Family Hubs open across Cambridgeshire
Cambridgeshire County Council has launched five new Best Start Family Hubs, including a site in Wisbech. These centres replace existing child and family facilities, bringing services like health, childcare, housing, and financial advice under one roof. While currently focused on support from pregnancy to age five, the service will eventually expand to assist young people up to age 19, or 25 for those with special educational needs.
The hubs are free to use and open to all families. Launch events are being held at each location throughout this week, offering residents the chance to meet staff and explore the available resources. Further information is also accessible through the council’s network of local sites and online services.

item.title: West Norfolk woman completes Ben Nevis climb for hospital unit
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk woman completes Ben Nevis climb for hospital unit
A West Norfolk woman has raised over £540 for the Peddars Way end-of-life unit at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Jan Mick climbed Ben Nevis in memory of her father, Harry, who passed away earlier this month.
The challenge took nine hours and 20 minutes to complete, with Jan facing difficult conditions including strong winds, rain, and temperatures dropping to minus four degrees at the summit. Jan, who recently moved to the area from Hertfordshire, chose the climb to honour her father’s active lifestyle. The hospital has expressed its gratitude for the donation, which exceeded the original £200 target. Supporters can still contribute to the fundraiser online.

item.title: Norfolk health officials consider future of A&E services
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk health officials consider future of A&E services
Health officials in Norfolk are considering plans that could see A&E units at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn and the James Paget Hospital in Gorleston closed. Confidential documents reveal three potential options for future emergency care, with only one retaining full A&E services at all three of the county’s hospitals. Other proposals include downgrading the units to urgent treatment centres or removing major trauma services.
The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group states that no final decisions have been made and that the documents are part of preliminary work. However, local MPs have expressed strong opposition to any potential downgrades, citing concerns over rural travel times and the impact on patient care.

The newsagent and stationer TG Jones has confirmed it will shut its Wisbech branch early next year. The shop, located on the Market Place, is scheduled to close its doors on Saturday, January 9, 2027. The closure is part of a wider, court-approved restructuring plan affecting several of the company's stores across the UK.
A spokesperson for the retailer expressed regret over the impact on the local community and staff. A closing down sale will be held at the premises before the final closure date. The company stated that its current priority is supporting affected employees while continuing to serve customers during the final weeks of operation.

Three-year driving ban for holidaymaker caught in King’s Lynn
A holidaymaker has been disqualified from driving for three years after being caught over the limit in King’s Lynn. Forty-two-year-old David Canatch, from Gainsborough, was stopped by police on Gayton Road after officers noticed his fog lights were on during clear weather. A breath test revealed he had 45 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath, exceeding the legal limit of 35.
Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Mr Canatch pleaded guilty to drink-driving. In addition to the driving ban, he was ordered to pay a £120 fine, a £48 victim surcharge, and £50 in court costs.

The infrastructure project, which cost 16,000 pounds, was completed before the decision to cut the local routes was made. Residents in the area are now facing a loss of public transport links despite the significant investment in the facilities.
